Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 13)
Topic: Rebirth Part III — Multiple Sukshma Shariras, Why "PastLife Siddhis" Are Really Your Own, and Why Universal Cosmos Energy Predates Every Named Devta

Source: Bhaiya's satsang session (video transcript, ~65 min), Mool Tattva series, continuing the "Life After Death" arc (Parts I and II covered separately). This session covers rebirth mechanics in depth and closes with a major cosmology teaching on the origin of named devtas. Purpose: Chatbot knowledge — English version.
1. REBIRTH HAS NO SINGLE FIXED CHANNEL

Rebirth does not follow one particular, identiﬁable channel — just as ther e can be multiple doors into the same room (or even breaking through a wall), rebirth can happen through many diﬀerent routes. This session focuses on explaining the underlying mechanics rather than a single ﬁx ed path.
2. THE BIG REVEAL — EVEN WHILE ALIVE, A DEVOTED
PRACTITIONER HAS MANY SUKSHMA SHARIRAS

A devoted practitioner (bhakt) does not have just one sukshma sharir (subtle body) — they have many , built up even during their current lifetime. Wherever you repeatedly perform an activity (especially jaap/sadhna), a sukshma sharir of yours remains there, continuing that same activity continuously. Illustration given: a sangat member who does heavy jaap has a sukshma sharir that stays at her place of practice, chanting continuously. When she astrally visits Ashaeiynn (with Baba's doots), her sukshma sharir tours the place — and if it lik es what it ﬁnds, a fragment (ansh) of that sukshma sharir can choose to stay behind permanently, while the rest returns with her. This is how a person can accumulate multiple, smaller sukshma shariras across diﬀer ent places and practices over a single lifetime. The MAIN sukshma sharir is whichever one corresponds to the activity you have repeated the most — it is the most active and dominant of the set.
3. WHAT HAPPENS AT DEATH

When someone leaves their body — in any cir cumstance, including sudden death — the atma tattva merges directly into paramatma tattva. What remains and lingers is the sukshma sharir — and this lingering sukshma sharir is exactly what is called "bhoot-pret." A sukshma sharir will typically remain wandering at the place of death. However, if the person was genuinely devoted (a bhakt) in life, the sukshma sharir that was already stationed elsewhere doing continuous jaap immediately coordinates with the newly wandering one and pulls it in — the ener gy in both bodies connects and syncs. This pull is not 100% complete — a fragment can r emain at the death site even as the main sukshma sharir is drawn toward wherever the person's ongoing devotion was seated. This directly corrects the older, imprecise idea that "devtas show mercy to a devotee after death." In reality, it is the devotee's OWN accumulated sukshma shariras (built through their own past devotion) that do this pulling-together — not an external act of divine favor.
4. SUKSHMA SHARIR SIZE VARIES WITH ASTRAL STRENGTH

The size of a sukshma sharir is not ﬁx ed — it depends on the person's strength in the astral world, however that strength was built (whether through practices like nonvegetarian/tantric methods, or through blessed, sattvic energy). It can visibly shrink or grow depending on context (for instance, appearing smaller in one setting and larger near a powerful presence), typically accompanied by a felt "gust of shakti" (shakti ka jhonka).
5. WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENS AT REBIRTH

At the moment of rebirth, all of a person's accumulated sukshma shariras (built across many activities and practices) contribute to forming ONE main tattva — and it is this tattva, not the sukshma shariras themselves, that moves forward into the new birth. The individual sukshma shariras themselves do NOT get "promoted" or physically move on — they r emain exactly where they are/were, continuing to exist. Both the remaining sukshma shariras and the newly forward-moving tattva exist simultaneously, in parallel. At conception, this forward-moving tattva (carrying the person's atma/prana tattva) reunites with a new physical body in the womb. A fresh set of sukshma shariras then begins to be built anew for this new body, as the person resumes sadhna/jaap in the new life. The panch tattva (ﬁve-element) body is speciﬁcally capable of generating sukshma shariras this way — with the right method and shakti, this same principle can even "put life into a stone."
6. OLD SUKSHMA SHARIRAS RETURN AS DIMENSION RISES

As the reborn person resumes jaap (especially under guru sanidhya), their kundalini shakti rises, and their dimension climbs. Whenever this rising dimension matches or crosses a dimension where one of the person's OLD sukshma shariras (from a past life, built through the same underlying lineage) already exists, that old sukshma sharir immediately recognizes them ("arre main hi hoon! tu mera, main tera") and rejoins/merges with the current practitioner, becoming part of their present siddhis. This is the real explanation behind what people commonly call "past-life siddhis suddenly manifesting." They are not new blessings freshly granted — they are literally the person's own accumulated sukshma shariras from earlier lifetimes, reuniting as current dimension rises to meet them.
7. BOTH GOOD AND BAD SUKSHMA SHARIRAS RETURN — WHY ONGOING SADHNA MATTERS

Across many lifetimes, a person's accumulated sukshma shariras are not uniformly positive — some may correspond to negative past actions of any kind (any karma is possible across lifetimes). As dimension rises, both positive and negative sukshma shariras can return and reconnect — "negative bhi aayenge, positive bhi aayenge." The saying "tera hi karm tujhe khaega ek din" (your own karma will consume you one day) describes exactly this mechanism — your own r eturning, previously-negative sukshma shariras.

The critical safeguard: keep your ongoing mantra shakti active in your CURRENT/existing body. If sadhna/bhakti continues without interruption, even a reuniting negative sukshma sharir gets puriﬁed/cleaned by the ongoing mantra shakti (in Ram's name) and converts into usable, positive power — since it was always the practitioner's own energy to begin with. If practice is abandoned, the same reuniting sukshma shariras can instead dominate and overwhelm the person rather than serve them.
8. THE UNEXPLAINED-GOOD-FORTUNE CASE

Some people who do no worship at all nonetheless ﬂourish ine xplicably ("unka bahut accha chalta hai"). The explanation: at some point (often via an unexpected blessing, such as a temple visit), one of their past-life sukshma shariras was suddenly triggered/awakened — pulling in nearby sukshma-sharir -level entities of a matching dimension (the example given is a "chudail"/negativity attaching in this way). Such an attached entity typically helps BOTH positively and negatively at once — genuinely aiding the person's material aﬀairs, which is e xactly why an outside observer (with drishti) checking on them may see a negativity present, while the person themselves feels nothing is wrong, since it is materially beneﬁting them. This is oﬀer ed as the real mechanism behind otherwise-baﬄing "unear ned luck."
9. HUMANS CAN MULTIPLY SUKSHMA SHARIRAS; ANIMALS CANNOT

Humans are described as a special tattva uniquely capable of BUILDING and MULTIPLYING sukshma shariras through repeated sadhna/activity. Animals and birds also have sukshma shariras, but lack the capacity to build or replicate them the way humans can. (This topic is ﬂagged as one to e xplore further once a practitioner's own drishti opens.)
10. FAMILY UPLIFTMENT EXPLAINED

The common saying that one devoted family member ("ek bhakt nikal jaave") uplifts the whole family, or "seven generations are saved," is explained through sukshma sharir mechanics: a mother's and child's sukshma sharira are fundamentally linked (essentially one) — so as a child's practice raises their own dimension, the connected parental sukshma sharir automatically rises along with it ("wo nikla toh yeh chadh gaye"). Bhaiya conﬁr ms the parent-upliftment logic directly, while noting some uncertainty about the speciﬁc "seven generations" e xtension. In the example of a couple both doing sadhna in hopes of a "tejasvi putra" (radiant/devoted son), the strength of the resulting child/rebirth depends on their combined tapobal

(intensity of sadhna) at that time — a soul/devata pending a human body is drawn according to the parents' combined sukshma-sharir "chain" and tapobal, eﬀectively pulled toward that family by the accumulated force of their practice.
11. THE COSMOLOGY REVEAL — UNIVERSAL COSMOS ENERGY PREDATES EVERY NAMED DEVTA

A guided sequence of questions in this session establishes a foundational teaching: did Universal Cosmos Energy (also called Brahm, or akashvani) come ﬁrst, or did named devtas like Hanuman Ji Maharaj or Bhagwan Shiv come ﬁrst? The answer given: the universal, all-pervading cosmos energy came ﬁrst — existing since time immemorial, before any named deity. Named devtas (Shiv, Narayan, and others) are described as beings who, at some point, began to grasp/absorb (grahan karna) this pre-existing universal energy — for instance, "a person named Shankar" began absorbing this universal energy speciﬁcally in the form later known as Shiv Tattva (which appears blue-colored in the astral world, as seen at Kailash). Supporting evidence cited: Bhagwan Shiv himself telling Mata Parvati, "hamare naseeb mein rajmahal nahi hai, hum toh fakir hain" ("we are not destined for palaces, we are a wandering ascetic") — implying that Shiv, too, was at some point in a mor e limited form before fully attaining his current, realized status, by absorbing and channeling this same pre-existing universal energy. The same logic is extended to Narayan, Ganesh, Krishna, and every other pujniya (worshipped) devi-devata — the universal cosmos ener gy predates and underlies all of them equally; each named deity is a speciﬁc being who began channeling it in their own particular way.
12. "WE ARE ALL DESCENDANTS OF SHIV, NARAYAN, AND HANUMAN" — WHY THIS IS LITERAL

Because all named devtas' sukshma shariras ultimately trace back to this SAME universal source energy, over time their respective sukshma shariras "replicated," intermingled with each other, and descendant lineages emerged from these combinations. This is why it is coherent — not merely poetic — to sa y "I am Shiv's child" AND "I am Narayan's child" AND "I am Hanuman's child" all at once: these lineages of sukshma shariras all trace back to, and intermingle from, the same one original universal energy. Whichever mantra/tattva a person practices, that speciﬁc sukshma-sharir lineage within them becomes more awakened and active. This is oﬀer ed as the deeper reason behind the saying "Shiv kahe pehle Ram bolo, Ram kahe pehle Shiv bolo" (say Ram's
name before Shiv's, and Shiv's name before Ram's) — the two names function as near - synonyms of each other in this framework.
13. WHY THE SAME UNIVERSAL ENERGY APPEARS IN DIFFERENT COLORS/FORMS

If the underlying energy is genuinely one and shared, why does it appear diﬀer ently for diﬀer ent devtas (e.g., Shiv's energy blue, Narayan's and Hanuman's each distinct)? A sangat member oﬀered that each devta/sadhak resonates at a diﬀerent frequency/vibration, producing distinct colors and forms even from one shared underlying energy — diﬀer ent tasks requiring diﬀer ent speciﬁc fr equencies. Bhaiya did not fully conﬁrm or resolve this in the session, treating it as a thread to be clariﬁed further in a future session — so this speciﬁc point should be pr esented as a plausible, oﬀer ed explanation rather than settled doctrine.
14. YOUR SADHNA LITERALLY FEEDS YOUR DEVTA'S OWN SHAKTI

Because a practitioner's own sukshma shariras are, in this framework, literally drawn from and identical-in-kind to a given devta's own replicated essence, intense sadhna by many practitioners directly increases that devta's own shakti — "jitna zyada log sadhna karte hain, utni Mahadev ki shakti badh rahi hai, kyunki sukshma sharir toh unhi ke hain." Devotional practice is framed here as a two-way current, not one-directional appeal. This is also oﬀer ed as the explanation for why devoted sadhaks occasionally have vivid visionary experiences of literally seeing themselves AS their chosen devta (for instance, "main Shiv ko pranam kar raha hoon, Shiv mujhe pranam kar rahe hain, aur main khud Shiv dikh raha hoon," or seeing oneself as Hanuman Ji, or as one's own Guru at other moments) — because one's own sukshma sharir is, in a structural sense, drawn from and of the same kind as that devta's own replicated essence.
15. WHY YOU SEE YOUR SPECIFIC ISHTA DEVTA AS YOUR PERSONAL SIDDHI

Given that everyone's sukshma shariras ultimately trace to the same universal source, why does a speciﬁc practitioner see a speciﬁc devta (for Ashaeiynn members, typically Hanuman Ji Maharaj) as their own personal siddhi, rather than some other deity? The answer depends on which speciﬁc past-life sukshma-sharir lineage the person happens to carry and reconnect with. If, in a past life, a person's sukshma sharir was built speciﬁcally thr ough devotion to Hanuman Ji, then as their current dimension rises to match where that particular sukshma sharir exists, it is Hanuman Ji's tattva/form

speciﬁcally that "returns" as their siddhi — not because Hanuman "chose" them fr om outside, but because that is literally which of their own accumulated lineages is being reawakened. The speciﬁc mantra practiced in the cur rent life further reinforces and awakens whichever sukshma-sharir lineage corresponds to that mantra/tattva. Siddhis, in this framework, are literally the practitioner's own property — not gif ts bestowed as an external favor, but one's own past accumulated sukshma shariras returning as current dimension rises to meet them. The devotional refrain "Baba, hum tumhare hain" is treated as deeply literal in this framework rather than merely metaphorical: since the energy Hanuman Ji Maharaj draws from the universal source and the energy falling on a devoted, dimension-matched practitioner is, in substance, the same — only the "vessel"/scale diﬀers ("hamari k attori choti hai" — our vessel is smaller, not the substance itself).
16. THE WARNING — PRACTITIONERS WHO STOP GET CONSUMED BY THEIR OWN SIDDHIS

A person's own returning sukshma shariras/siddhis (both good and bad) stay under control only as long as the practitioner keeps drawing on and channeling the universal cosmic energy through ongoing sadhna. If a practitioner lets go of this — stops their mantra practice/sadhna — their own accumulated siddhis can begin to control THEM instead, sometimes described colloquially as such a person eventually "going crazy" or being consumed by their own power ("unhi ki siddhiyan unhi ko khane lagti hain"). This is oﬀered as the real explanation behind the folk observation that certain pandits or practitioners "used to be good, but have gone mad" over time — not external possession, but their own accumulated power turning uncontained once ongoing practice stopped.
17. MANY PATHS AWAKEN A SUKSHMA SHARIR — NOT MANTRA ALONE

Mantra jaap is only one of several valid methods for awakening a sukshma sharir. Others include: direct grace/transmission from a Guru, sound and vibration practices more generally, speciﬁc physical exercises/practices, and dhyana (meditation). Multiple legitimate paths exist toward the same underlying goal.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

1. Rebirth has no single ﬁx ed channel/route — many diﬀer ent paths are possible. 2. Even during one lifetime, a devoted practitioner accumulates MANY sukshma shariras — wherever an activity/jaap is repeated, a piece of them remains there, continuing it.

3. At death, the atma tattva merges into paramatma tattva; the lingering sukshma sharir becomes what is called bhoot-pret. A devotee's other, already-active sukshma shariras (from ongoing jaap elsewhere) actively pull the wandering one toward them — not full mer cy from an external devta, but the person's own accumulated devotion at work. 4. Sukshma sharir size varies with astral-world strength and context, often felt as a "gust of shakti." 5. At rebirth, all accumulated sukshma shariras contribute to ONE forward-moving tattva; the individual sukshma shariras themselves stay behind and continue existing in parallel. A new body builds fresh sukshma shariras as sadhna resumes. 6. As dimension rises through renewed sadhna, OLD sukshma shariras (from past lives, matching that dimension) rejoin the practitioner — this, not fr esh external blessing, is the real mechanism behind "past-life siddhis." 7. Both positive AND negative past sukshma shariras can return as dimension rises; ongoing mantra shakti in the current body is what puriﬁes a r eturning negative one into usable power — stopping practice risks the r everse, being overwhelmed by one's own returning karma. 8. Inexplicable, unearned good fortune is often explained by a past-life sukshma sharir suddenly reawakened (e.g., via an unexpected blessing), pulling in a matching-dimension entity that helps both materially and, often invisibly, negatively at once. 9. Humans can build and multiply sukshma shariras through repeated practice; animals/birds have sukshma shariras but cannot replicate them this way. 10. A devoted child's rising dimension automatically lifts a linked parent's sukshma sharir too — the real mechanism behind "one devoted child uplifts the family." 11. Universal Cosmos Energy (Brahm) predates every named devta; named devtas are beings who began absorbing/channeling this pre-existing energy in their own particular form (e.g., Shiv Tattva, seen as blue in the astral world). 12. Because named devtas' sukshma shariras all trace to this same source and intermingled over time, it is literally coherent to say "I am the child of Shiv, Narayan, AND Hanuman" simultaneously — not just a devotional ﬁgur e of speech. 13. Intense sadhna by practitioners directly increases the corresponding devta's own shakti, since the practitioner's sukshma shariras are drawn from that devta's own replicated essence — devotion is a two-way current. 14. Which speciﬁc devta appears as a person's personal siddhi depends on which past-life sukshma-sharir lineage they carry and reconnect with — siddhis ar e literally one's own returning property, not externally bestowed gifts. 15. Practitioners who stop drawing on universal cosmic energy (stop sadhna) risk being controlled/overwhelmed by their own accumulated siddhis rather than controlling them — oﬀer ed as the real explanation for practitioners who "went mad" over time. 16. Mantra jaap is one of several valid paths to awaken a sukshma sharir — Guru's grace, sound/vibration, speciﬁc e xercises, and meditation are all also valid.
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 13, English)
Rebirth Part III — Multiple Sukshma Shariras and the Origin of Named Devtas
User-style questions with answers grounded in Bhaiya's discourse. Greeting style: "Jai Siya Ram."

Q1. Does rebirth happen through one speciﬁc, identiﬁable channel? A: Jai Siya Ram! No — r ebirth doesn't follow a single ﬁx ed route, any more than a room has only one door. There are multiple paths by which rebirth can occur; this session focuses on the underlying mechanics rather than one ﬁx ed channel.

Q2. Do I only have one sukshma sharir (subtle body), even while I'm alive? A: No — a devoted practitioner accumulates MANY sukshma shariras even during their current lifetime. Wherever you repeatedly do an activity, especially jaap or sadhna, a sukshma sharir of yours remains there, continuing that activity. If it "likes" a place it visits (for instance, during an astral visit to Ashaeiynn), a fragment of it can even choose to stay behind permanently while the rest returns with you. The MAIN sukshma sharir is whichever one corresponds to your most-repeated activity.

Q3. What actually happens to someone right after they die? A: The atma tattva merges directly into paramatma tattva. What remains and lingers is the sukshma sharir — and that lingering sukshma sharir is exactly what gets called "bhoot-pret." It typically wanders near the place of death.

Q4. If someone was very devoted in life but died suddenly, does their devotion help them after death? A: Yes, directly — but not the way it's usually described. If the person was genuinely devoted, the sukshma sharir already stationed elsewhere doing continuous jaap immediately coordinates with the newly wandering one and pulls it in, since the energy in both bodies connects. This pull isn't 100% complete — a fragment can r emain at the death site even as the main sukshma sharir is drawn toward wherever their devotion was seated. This corrects the imprecise old idea that "devtas show mercy to a devotee after death" — it's r eally the person's OWN accumulated sukshma shariras doing the pulling, not an external act of favor.

Q5. Why do some people's sukshma shariras look bigger or more powerful than others? A: Sukshma sharir size depends on the person's strength in the astral world, however that strength was built — thr ough blessed, sattvic practice or through other means like tantric practices. It can visibly shrink or grow depending on context, often accompanied by a felt "gust of shakti."

Q6. What actually happens at the moment of rebirth — do all my sukshma shariras move forward together? A: No — this is a k ey distinction. All of a person's accumulated sukshma shariras contribute to forming ONE main tattva, and it is only this tattva that moves forward into the new birth. The individual sukshma shariras themselves do NOT get "promoted" or physically move — they stay e xactly where they are, continuing to exist in parallel with the newly forward-moving tattva. At conception, that tattva reunites with a new physical body, and a fresh set of sukshma shariras begins building anew as the new person resumes sadhna.

Q7. People sometimes suddenly manifest what looks like "past-life siddhis." What's really happening? A: This is one of the session's central reveals. As a reborn person resumes jaap and their dimension rises, whenever that dimension matches or crosses one where an OLD sukshma sharir of theirs (from a past life) already exists, that old sukshma sharir immediately recognizes them and rejoins them, becoming part of their present siddhis. What looks like a "past-life siddhi suddenly manifesting" is literally the person's own accumulated sukshma sharir reuniting with them as their current dimension rises to meet it — not a fr esh external blessing.

Q8. Are all the sukshma shariras that come back to me necessarily good ones? A: No, and this matters a lot. Across many lifetimes, a person's accumulated sukshma shariras aren't uniformly positive — some cor respond to negative past actions. As dimension rises, both positive and negative sukshma shariras can return and reconnect. The saying "tera hi karm tujhe khaega ek din" (your own karma will consume you one day) describes exactly this mechanism.

Q9. How do I make sure a returning negative sukshma sharir doesn't harm me? A: Keep your ongoing mantra shakti active in your current body — don't stop your practice. If sadhna continues without interruption, even a reuniting negative sukshma sharir gets puriﬁed by your ongoing mantra shakti and converts into usable, positive power, since it was always your own energy anyway. If you abandon your practice, the same reuniting sukshma shariras can dominate and overwhelm you instead of serving you.

Q10. Some people who never worship at all seem to have inexplicably good fortune. How? A: Often, at some point (commonly via an unexpected blessing, like a temple visit), one of their past-life sukshma shariras was suddenly triggered — pulling in a nearby entity of matching dimension (the session gives the example of a "chudail"/negativity attaching this way). Such an attached entity typically helps both materially AND, often invisibly, negatively at the same time — which is why an outside observer with drishti might see a negativity pr esent, while the person themselves feels nothing is wrong, since it's genuinely beneﬁting their material aﬀairs.

Q11. Do animals and birds have sukshma shariras too? A: Yes, they do — but unlik e humans, they cannot build or multiply their sukshma shariras through repeated activity or practice. Humans are described as a uniquely capable tattva in this respect. (This is a topic to explore further once a practitioner's own drishti opens.)

Q12. People say one devoted child in a family can uplift the whole family, even "seven generations." Is this literal? A: There's a real mechanism behind it. A mother's and child's sukshma sharira are fundamentally linked — essentially one — so as a child's practice raises their own dimension, the connected parental sukshma sharir automatically rises along with it. The parent-upliftment part is conﬁr med directly; the speciﬁc "seven generations" e xtension is treated with more uncertainty. In cases where both parents do sadhna hoping for a "tejasvi putra," the strength of the resulting child depends on their combined tapobal at that time.

Q13. Which came ﬁrst — Universal Cosmos Energy , or named devtas like Hanuman Ji Maharaj and Bhagwan Shiv? A: Universal Cosmos Energy (also called Brahm, or akashvani) came ﬁrst — it is described as all-pervading and e xisting since time immemorial, before any named deity. Named devtas are described as beings who, at some point, began to grasp and absorb this pre-existing universal energy in their own particular form — for instance, "a person named Shankar" began absorbing it as what came to be known as Shiv Tattva (which appears blue-colored in the astral world, as seen at Kailash).

Q14. Is there evidence that Bhagwan Shiv himself was once in a more limited or "human" state? A: The session points to Bhagwan Shiv's own words to Mata Parvati — "hamar e naseeb mein rajmahal nahi hai, hum toh fakir hain" ("we are not destined for palaces, we are a wandering ascetic") — as suggesting he too was, at some point, in a mor e limited form before fully attaining his current realized status by absorbing and channeling the pre-existing universal energy. The same logic is extended to Narayan, Ganesh, Krishna, and every other worshipped devi-devata.

Q15. Can I really say I'm the child of Shiv, of Narayan, and of Hanuman Ji all at the same time? A: Yes, and this is meant literally, not just poetically, in this framework. Because all named devtas' sukshma shariras ultimately trace back to the same Universal Cosmos Energy, their respective sukshma shariras "replicated" and intermingled over time, and descendant lineages emerged from these combinations. Whichever mantra/tattva you practice, that speciﬁc sukshma-sharir lineage within you becomes more awakened — which is also the deeper r eason behind the saying "Shiv kahe pehle Ram bolo, Ram kahe pehle Shiv bolo."

Q16. If the underlying energy is really one and shared, why does it look diﬀerent in color/form for diﬀerent devtas? A: One explanation oﬀer ed in the session is that each devta/sadhak resonates at a diﬀer ent frequency or vibration, producing distinct colors and forms even from a shared underlying energy — diﬀer ent tasks needing diﬀer ent speciﬁc fr equencies. This wasn't fully resolved or conﬁr med as settled doctrine in this session — it's a thr ead Bhaiya said would be clariﬁed further later, so it should be tr eated as a plausible, oﬀer ed explanation rather than ﬁnal teaching.

Q17. Does my own personal sadhna actually do anything for my devta, or is it purely one-directional (me asking, devta giving)? A: It's described as a two-way current. Because a practitioner's own sukshma shariras are, in this framework, drawn from and identical-in-kind to their devta's own replicated essence, intense sadhna by many practitioners directly increases that devta's own shakti — "jitna zyada log sadhna k arte hain, utni Mahadev ki shakti badh rahi hai."

Q18. Why do I speciﬁcally see Hanuman Ji Maharaj in visions and feel him as my personal siddhi, rather than some other devta? A: It depends on which speciﬁc past-life sukshma-sharir lineage you happen to carry and reconnect with. If, in a past life, your sukshma sharir was built speciﬁcally thr ough devotion to Hanuman Ji, then as your current dimension rises to match where that sukshma sharir exists, it is speciﬁcally his tattva/for m that "returns" as your siddhi — not because he e xternally "chose" you, but because that's literally which of your own accumulated lineages is reawakening. Your current mantra practice further reinforces that same lineage. Siddhis, in this sense, are literally your own returning property — this is why the devotional line "Baba, hum tumhare hain" is meant quite literally: the energy falling on Hanuman Ji and on a devoted, dimension-matched practitioner is, in substance, the same — only the vessel/scale diﬀers ("hamari k attori choti hai").

Q19. Is it dangerous to ever stop my sadhna once I've built up strong siddhis? A: Yes — this is an important warning. A person's own returning siddhis (both good and bad) stay under control only as long as ongoing sadhna keeps channeling universal cosmic energy through them. If a practitioner lets go of this and stops their practice, their own accumulated siddhis can begin to control THEM instead — described colloquially as such a person eventually "going crazy" or being consumed by their own power. This is oﬀer ed as the real explanation behind the folk observation that certain pandits or practitioners "used to be good, but have gone mad" over time.

Q20. Is mantra jaap the only way to awaken a sukshma sharir? A: No — it's one of several valid methods. Others include direct grace/transmission from a Guru, sound and vibration practices more generally, speciﬁc physical e xercises, and dhyana (meditation). Multiple legitimate paths lead toward the same underlying goal.
Bot Response Guidelines (Session 13 additions)

When a user describes suddenly feeling powerful, gifted, or "chosen" by a speciﬁc devta, use the sukshma-sharir-reunion framing rather than "the devta blessed you externally" — this is the session's central correction, and should be applied consistently. Q. Bhaiya, Ashaeiynn ke doot kaise dikhte hain? Sabko ek jaise dikhte hain kya? A: "Bhai jo dwar pe hai woh alag hai, jo aapke peeche baithe hain unka saiz alag hota hai. Phir jab hum andar jaate hain, jahan hawan chal raha hota hai, wahan bahut saare sukshma sharir hote hain, bahut saare sadhu sant hote hain, doot bhi hote hain. Sabke haath mein astra-shastra hote hain, aur har cheez ke liye alag doot rakhe gaye hain — negativity k e kaam ke liye alag doot hain, raksha suraksha ke liye alag hain. (Naya, vivid detail — users ko Ashaeiynn ke astral structure ki ek clear tasveer deta hai, aur reassuring bhi hai ki doot hamesha karuna se dekhte hain.)

Q. Bhaiya, kisi ka kuch nahi karta phir bhi uska sab kaam ban jaata hai — aisa kyun hota hai? A: "Kabhi-kabhi kuch log pooja paath nahi karte, unka bahut accha chalta hai. Aur woh jagrit aise hi nahi hota — kisi mandir mein gaye, k ahin se aashirwad mil gaya, jaise hi aashirwad mila unki kundalini shakti ekdum se uthi toh jis dimension mein aaspaas unke sukshma sharir the woh khinch gaye. Ek shakti aa gayi — maan lo ek chudail aa gayi. Ab woh chudail jo hai balle-balle kar deti hai unki cheezon ki. Matlab sab kaam hone lagta hai unka. Koi aur checking karega toh bolega bhai chudail dikh rahi hai yaar, woh kahega yaar mera toh sab sahi chal raha hai. Aur pata hai aise log khud se checking nahi karvate — ink o inki checking doosre aakar karte hain." (Bahut relatable aur naya fact — "kisi ki kismat achanak chamak jaana" ka ek concrete, nonjudgmental explanation, jo bahut logon ke sawaal ka jawab deta hai.)
